claims.text: Greater exposure to ultra-processed foods is directly associated with a higher risk of incident cardiovascular disease related mortality (risk ratio 1.50, 95% confidence interval 1.37 to 1.63).
Greater dose-response exposure to ultra-processed foods is directly associated with a higher risk of incident type 2 diabetes (risk ratio 1.12, 95% confidence interval 1.11 to 1.13).
Greater exposure to ultra-processed foods is directly associated with higher odds of prevalent anxiety outcomes (odds ratio 1.48, 95% confidence interval 1.37 to 1.59).
Greater exposure to ultra-processed foods is directly associated with higher odds of prevalent combined common mental disorder outcomes (odds ratio 1.53, 95% confidence interval 1.43 to 1.63).
Greater non-dose-response exposure to ultra-processed foods is directly associated with a higher risk of incident all cause mortality (risk ratio 1.21, 95% confidence interval 1.15 to 1.27).
Direct associations were found between exposure to ultra-processed foods and 32 out of 45 (71%) evaluated health parameters.

evidence.description: Convincing evidence (class I) supported direct associations between greater ultra-processed food exposure and higher risks of incident cardiovascular disease related mortality (risk ratio 1.50, 95% confidence interval 1.37 to 1.63; GRADE=very low).
Convincing evidence (class I) supported direct associations with type 2 diabetes (dose-response risk ratio 1.12, 1.11 to 1.13; moderate).
Convincing evidence (class I) supported direct associations with higher risks of prevalent anxiety outcomes (odds ratio 1.48, 1.37 to 1.59; low).
Convincing evidence supported combined common mental disorder outcomes (odds ratio 1.53, 1.43 to 1.63; low).

Highly suggestive (class II) evidence indicated that greater exposure to ultra-processed foods was directly associated with higher risks of incident all cause mortality (risk ratio 1.21, 1.15 to 1.27; low).

Overall, direct associations were found between exposure to ultra-processed foods and 32 (71%) health parameters spanning mortality, cancer, and mental, respiratory, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, and metabolic health outcomes.

methodologies.name: Systematic Umbrella Review and Random-Effects Re-Meta-Analysis
methodologies.description: Systematic synthesis and statistical re-analysis of meta-analyses of observational epidemiological studies evaluating associations between Nova ultra-processed food exposure and adverse health outcomes.

limitations.text: As a high-level umbrella review, this work did not consider specific confounder or mediator adjustments and sensitivity analyses across primary studies.
Inclusion of original research articles with varied methods of dietary assessment introduces dietary measurement bias.
Observational epidemiological studies included in the review have inherent risk of residual confounding.
The Nova food classification system faces criticism regarding potential imprecision and inconsistency among evaluators.

future_work.text: Urgent mechanistic research to clarify physiological pathways linking ultra-processed foods to adverse health outcomes.
Development and evaluation of population-based and public health strategies to target and reduce dietary exposure to ultra-processed foods.
Short-term randomized controlled trials testing the effects of ultra-processed food exposure on intermediate health outcomes such as inflammation, gut microbiome, and insulin resistance.
